drivingQuestion: How does water in a pit count toward the lethal ten handbreadths?
outcomeNote: The dictum stands; both dilemmas remain unresolved

segments.he: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָּא: בּוֹר שְׁמוֹנָה, וּמֵהֶן שְׁנֵי טְפָחִים מַיִם – חַיָּיב. מַאי טַעְמָא? כֹּל טֶפַח דְּמַיָּא – כִּתְרֵי דְיַבָּשָׁה דָּמֵי.
segments.en: § «Rabba bar bar Ḥana says» that «Shmuel bar Marta says:» With regard to «a pit» that is «eight» handbreadths deep and «two handbreadths of it» contain «water,» one is «liable» for it. «What is the reason? Each handbreadth of water is like two» handbreadths «of dry space.» Therefore, the pit is effectively ten handbreadths in depth and contains a sufficient quantity of lethal fumes to render its owner liable.

segments.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: בּוֹר תִּשְׁעָה וּמֵהֶן טֶפַח אֶחָד מַיִם, מַהוּ? מִי אָמְרִינַן כֵּיוָן דְּלָא נְפִישִׁי מַיָּא – לֵית בֵּיהּ הַבְלָא; אוֹ דִלְמָא, כֵּיוָן דְּעַמִּיק טְפֵי – אִית בֵּיהּ הַבְלָא?
segments.en: «A dilemma was raised before» the Sages: If «a pit» is «nine» handbreadths deep, «and from that» measurement, «one handbreadth» contains «water, what is» the halakha? Is this case equivalent to the previous one? «Do we say» that «since» there is «not» as «large» a quantity of «water» as in the case stated by Rabba bar bar Ḥana, the pit «does not have» a sufficient quantity of lethal «fumes» to render the digger liable? «Or perhaps» it can be argued that «since» the pit is «deeper» than the one in the previous case, «it does have» lethal «fumes,» despite containing less water?

segments.he: בּוֹר שִׁבְעָה, וּמֵהֶן שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים מַיִם, מַהוּ? מִי אָמְרִינַן כֵּיוָן דִּנְפִישִׁי מַיִם טְפֵי – אִית בֵּיהּ הַבְלָא; אוֹ דִלְמָא, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא עַמִּקָא – לֵית בֵּיהּ הַבְלָא? תֵּיקוּ.
segments.en: Similarly, the following question can be raised: «What is» the halakha if «a pit» is «seven» handbreadths deep «and three of the handbreadths» contain «water? Do we say» that «since» there is a «much larger» quantity «of water» in this case, it is equivalent to a pit of ten handbreadths and therefore «has» lethal «fumes, or perhaps since it is not» as «deep, it does not have» a sufficient quantity of lethal «fumes» to render the digger liable? The Gemara concludes: The question «shall stand» unresolved.
